tts.stopConfirmTitle: What should happen to the server?
tts.stopConfirmBody: The Fish Speech server is running and holds roughly 17 GB of graphics memory. Stopping frees it; any playback in progress ends at once. Restarting stops it as well and brings it straight back up — the way to go when it is running but no longer answering properly. Either way the next sentence takes up to two minutes, because the model has to load again. Sentences already spoken stay in the cache and can still be played without a server.
tts.stopConfirmBodyStarting: The server is starting up and taking more graphics memory as it goes — up to roughly 17 GB. Stopping now ends the startup at once and frees everything it has taken. All you lose is the loading time spent so far; a later start begins again from scratch.

settings.idleMinutesDescription: 0 means the server is never stopped automatically.

settings.compileDescription: Synthesis ALWAYS runs on the GPU — this switch only toggles the compile acceleration (~9× faster, RTF ~0.65 instead of ~6) at the cost of ~60 s longer server startup. Takes effect on the next server start; there is no CPU mode.
settings.volumeDescription: Playback volume for speech output, independent of feedback sounds.
settings.normalizeDescription: Levels every voice to the same loudness (-20 LUFS) — when recording or importing a reference and during playback. Without it, one speaker in a dialogue is too quiet and the next too loud.
settings.prewarmDescription: Brings the Fish Speech server up as soon as the app opens. It does not shorten the minute or so of loading — it runs while you are pasting a text or picking a voice anyway. Off by default, because the server takes roughly 17 GB of graphics memory while it does.
settings.enhanceDescription: Removes rumble and mains hum, lowers the noise in speaking pauses and evens out loud and quiet passages. Applies in three places: when recording or importing a voice, during playback, and when saving to a file. It matters most at recording time — Fish Speech models the voice from that take, including whatever is audible behind it.
settings.enhanceStrengthDescription: Gentle only cleans up and leaves the voice alone. Strong is for audibly noisy recordings and may colour the voice slightly.
settings.speedDescription: 0.5×–2×. Resampling slightly changes the pitch as well.
settings.flowHint: Pauses at commas, sentence ends and paragraph ends
settings.exportFormatDescription: Format for saved audio files (voice changer, summaries). The server encodes directly.
settings.exportBitrateDescription: Sound quality and file size of the MP3 export. 192 kbps is plenty for speech; higher settings only pay off for music.
settings.contextMenuDescription: Adds "Read with Local Voice AI" to the right-click menu of TXT/MD/PDF/DOCX files. Note: Windows offers no system-wide menu for selected text — use the clipboard hotkey for that.
settings.autoTranscribeDescription: When you record or pick a reference, the app produces the transcript itself and fills it in; it stays editable. Switched off, the field stays empty and the text has to be typed — without a matching text Fish Speech learns the voice from the wrong words.
settings.engineDescription: Fish Speech sounds more natural and uses the graphics card. Piper runs on the CPU, starts instantly and needs no server — at the cost of a plainer voice.

meetings.captureSystemDescription: Default for the “Capture system audio” checkbox when starting. The last choice on the recording page is remembered here.
meetings.autoEnhance: Create AI notes automatically after the meeting
meetings.autoEnhanceDescription: As soon as the transcript is complete after stopping, the AI builds the meeting notes from your notes and the transcript. Imports never trigger this. Nothing happens without a configured language-model provider.
meetings.defaultTemplateDescription: Template that is preselected for new meetings.
meetings.semanticSearchDescription: Finds meetings by meaning, not only by matching words – for search and chat. Needs the search model BGE-M3 (635 MB), which runs locally on this computer. The index is built in the background, never during a recording.
meetings.semanticSearchIndexDescription: The search model is only downloaded when you click the button. Without it, keyword search keeps working.
meetings.slideVisionDescription: Reads the text of detected slides once more with a local vision model (Gemma 4 E4B) – numbers and tables come out right – and describes every slide in one sentence. Needs a graphics card and the image projector (about 1 GB, only downloaded when you click the button). The model is loaded only for the slide job and unloaded afterwards. Without these requirements, Windows text recognition stays in use.
meetings.slideVisionStateDescription: The image projector is only downloaded when you click the button. Without it, slides are still read with Windows text recognition.
meetings.slideVisionNoGpu: No suitable graphics card found – Windows text recognition stays in use
meetings.slideVisionLowVram: Not enough free graphics memory (at least 6 GB) – Windows text recognition stays in use
meetings.slideVisionNoModel: Gemma 4 E4B is missing – download it under “Models”
meetings.echoCancellationDescription: Removes the other party, which comes back from your speakers into the microphone, from your track so it does not appear twice as “Me” in the transcript. Needs system audio as the reference. The raw microphone recording is kept unchanged. Takes effect from the next recording.
meetings.detectDescription: Notices when a program uses the microphone (Teams, Zoom, Webex, Slack, Discord, WhatsApp, Skype, Signal or a browser) and shows a hint. Only Windows' usage log is read, never the microphone itself. It only ever shows a hint and never starts recording on its own.
meetings.detectIgnoredDescription: Programs that never trigger a hint. Separate names with commas, for example "obs64.exe, Discord". Case does not matter and part of a name is enough.
meetings.diarizationDescription: After stopping, on import and on re-transcription, a local model detects who speaks when and labels the transcript with numbered speakers ("Gegenseite 1", "Person 2", ...). You can name the speakers in the transcript. Nothing that recognises a voice is stored. Takes effect from the next run.
meetings.diarizationModelDescription: NVIDIA Streaming Sortformer (NVIDIA Open Model License). Not shipped with the app; downloaded once here.
meetings.diarizationModelReadyHint: Model installed. "Re-transcribe" in the menu now separates the speakers.
meetings.diarizationModelCancelled: Download cancelled. It can be resumed later.
meetings.diarizationModelStatusFailed: Could not read the model status.
meetings.voiceSuggestionsDescription: Default: on, but only takes effect once the voice model is downloaded. When speaker separation splits one person into several speakers, the speaker table suggests merging them. Nothing is merged automatically and every merge can be split again. Voices are only compared within one meeting; the voiceprints stay in memory and are never stored.
meetings.voiceSuggestionsModelDescription: CAM++ (3D-Speaker, Apache-2.0) runs locally. It is only downloaded on request.
meetings.selfNameDescription: Your own name in the transcript: your microphone ("Me") and, if the microphone is split into several people, the speaker with the largest share always carry this name, even if nobody addresses you. In People you are marked as "me". Leave empty to keep "Me".

refineStream.label: Polish live text afterwards with Ollama
refineStream.description: While inserting live, a locally running Ollama polishes each sentence (grammar, punctuation, filler words) and replaces it in the target document. Numbers, negations, rare terms and word order are protected. If a sentence is not ready in time (4 s per sentence, 12 s at the end) or Ollama is not running, the original text stays. Ollama is never required for recording, recognition or insertion. Default: off.

lazyStreamClose.label: Keep Mic Open Between Dictations
lazyStreamClose.description: Keeps the microphone stream open for 5 minutes after recording stops. A freshly opened microphone delivers no audio for 0.2 to 0.6 seconds, so the first words were lost; with the stream open every following dictation starts instantly. May degrade Bluetooth audio quality while active.

dialog.title: Connect calendar
dialog.name: Name
dialog.privacy: The address grants read access to the whole calendar. It is stored encrypted (bound to your user account) on this computer and only sent to the calendar provider.
dialog.helpTitle: Where do I find the address?
dialog.outlookSteps: Settings → Calendar → Shared calendars → “Publish a calendar”. Pick the calendar, permission “Can view all details” (otherwise attendees are missing), “Publish” and copy the ICS link. If IT blocks publishing, the option does not appear. Published calendars refresh with a delay of a few hours, depending on the provider.
dialog.googleSteps: calendar.google.com → Settings → pick the calendar on the left → “Integrate calendar” → copy “Secret address in iCal format”. Do not share this address: anyone who knows it sees the whole calendar.
dialog.otherSteps: Share the calendar publicly or by link and paste the ICS or webcal link.

dictate.threeToggle: Press {{shortcut}} again – the text is inserted.
dictate.note: During a recording, {{cancel}} cancels the dictation without inserting text. Without a recording, {{cancel}} closes this introduction. Change the shortcut and mode (hold or toggle) under Settings › Dictation.

ki.erklaerung: The AI reaches files in two ways: directly (the assistant searches the file store) and through projects as context. “On” allows both ways. “Off” (also when nothing is set) blocks only the direct way; files stay usable as project context as long as they are switched on in the project. “Locked” blocks both ways and always wins, even over “On” in subfolders. The data class applies on top: “Personal data” never goes to cloud models, “Confidential” only to local models or by exception.
